object_description: compact symmetrical volume on the north-eastern edge with fully glazed facades
design_condition: the replacement building takes the north-eastern edge of the perimeter, oriented to the building it replaces, and creates a new address along the street with its clear presence

positive: The building creates a new address for the school with its clear presence along the street
Permeability and the obstructed views of the forest remain unchanged from the status quo
Existing outdoor space qualities of the old buildings are largely retained
The internal floor plan is organised symmetrically
The arrangement of the two stairwells is good both organisationally and for earthquake safety
Uses are grouped around central, multifunctional zones on all above-ground floors
Atriums added to the vertical access provide an interior accent and good lighting
The division into public uses on the ground floor and classrooms above is logical
Each classroom is directly assigned a group room that can also be used independently
The contemporary floor plans correspond to current developments and largely meet the requirements
Interventions in the listed pavilions are limited to the bare essentials and only in the interiors
Group rooms are arranged between two classrooms in a room divided by furniture to protect the fabric
A lift can easily be installed as part of the renovation of the toilet facilities
The opening of the day school to the south is correct and its location between the levels is interesting
Moving the janitor apartment to the upper floor gives it more privacy
The new building impresses with its compact volume and very simple insulation perimeter without weak points
The building technology concept with pellet heating and roof photovoltaics is compliant
Construction costs are in the medium range thanks to the compact building and selective interventions
Particularly convincing due to the efficient floor plans of the new building
The concentration on a new building at the north-eastern end of the perimeter is correct
negative: The entrance corner is obstructed rather than furnished by three plant troughs
The closed rear facade of the gymnasium is problematic for the quality of the courtyard
The connection between new building and elementary school playground along the sidewalk should be questioned
The all-round glazed facades are controversial as they suggest non-school uses
They are perceived more as a foreign body in the existing school complex
The adjoining rooms are mainly specialist classrooms where flexibility is less in demand
In the basement good lighting is only achieved through a ground slope on the northern facade
The day school opening could be more generous to suit the use
Its location makes access to common rooms in the new building more difficult
Without shading measures the risk of overheating remains
The proposed radiators appear rather complex in view of future district heating
The precise urban positioning, volumetric expansion and formal response fail to recognise the existing qualities
